display.purpose: Interior page nameplates only, one per page, seated on a 2px brass rule.

headline.purpose: The home statement of work; carries one italic serif phrase in amber.

title.purpose: Section headings, year headings, leading range name. Capped at 24ch, balanced.

subtitle.purpose: Card names, publication titles, range names.

reading.purpose: Literata: everything the operator says in sentences — prose, ledes, blurbs, venues.

body.purpose: List items, readouts, notes. Tabular figures throughout.

label.purpose: The instrument's own lettering: captions, column labels, group names, language tags. Never an eyebrow over a heading.

shadows.name: control-rest
shadows.purpose: The amber mailto control at rest — the only element in the system that sits above its surface.

shadows.name: control-pressed
shadows.purpose: The same control on :active, paired with translateY(1px).

shadows.name: bezel-inset
shadows.purpose: The portrait frame: a seated panel, not a moulded bevel.

shadows.name: lamp-glow
shadows.purpose: The lit indicator inside the control.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default for colour, border-colour and background state changes on links, ticks, cards and chips.

motion.name: surface
motion.purpose: Card background lift by one tonal step on hover.

motion.name: instrument
motion.purpose: The instrument easing: scale ticks growing (620ms) and the drawn arrow's 3px travel (160ms).

motion.name: lamp-pulse
motion.purpose: The lamp's slow breath. Wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, as is every animation here.

stickyBudget.note: Three layers stick at once. Each offsets by the sum of the ones above it; both tokens change at 720px because the chrome wraps to two rows.

contrastLedger.note: Computed WCAG ratios for every text pair in the build. Edits must not regress these below 4.5:1.

declaredButUnused.note: Present in instrument.css, referenced nowhere in the build. Not part of the recorded system; either wire them or drop them.

narrative.overview:
This surface is a measuring instrument, not a page about one. A precision instrument has a dark enamelled chassis and light engraved plates screwed into it; the chassis carries identity, navigation and structure, and the plates carry anything a visitor must actually read at length. Brass hairlines rule and graduate every division, exactly as they do on a machined faceplate. Amber is the lamp: it is spent only on live state, on lab-led publication ticks, and on the single action the whole site is built to produce — an email.

The system's central commitment is that every claim carries its tolerance stamped beside it. The publication scale is drawn from the real bibliography and would disappear if the data were removed; the software rack labels each tool STABLE, EXPERIMENTAL or DEPRECATED in the author's own vocabulary. Nothing here is a decorative gauge. Density is high and deliberately unpadded: rules and seams do the separating that whitespace and cards would do elsewhere.

The world refuses two category ruts by construction — the consultant hero with three service cards, and the faculty page with a sidebar headshot. It also refuses the ornaments that usually accompany them: no eyebrow or kicker above a heading, no section numbering, no metric strip of big round numbers, no Unicode glyph standing in for an icon, and no faked hardware bevels. The instrument look is earned with honest borders, flat fills and one restrained offset shadow, never with a skeuomorphic gradient.
keyCharacteristics: Two surfaces only: dark enamel chassis and cream engraved plate; a page alternates between them and nothing else.
Brass hairlines (1px) and heavy rules (2px) instead of shadows, cards or rounded containers.
Amber reserved: live state, lab-led ticks, the mailto control. Nothing else may take it.
Condensed uppercase Archivo engraves labels; Literata reads at length.
Square by default — the largest radius in the system is 2px.
Data-derived graphics: the scale is the bibliography, drawn.

rules.name: The Reserved Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means one of three things and nothing else: live state, a lab-led publication, or the single mailto action. If a new element wants amber for emphasis, it gets brass or a brighter cream instead.

rules.name: The Two Surfaces Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two backgrounds in this system — enamel and plate. Anything a visitor must read at length goes on a plate; identity, navigation, indexes and data graphics stay on the chassis. A third surface colour is a defect, not an option.

rules.name: The Brass Draws, Amber Lights Rule
rules.body: Every rule, border, graduation and divider is brass or brass-dim. Amber never draws structure and brass never fills a control.

rules.name: The Brass-Dim-On-Plate Rule
rules.body: Brass at full strength fails contrast on cream (2.8:1) and is therefore never used for text on a plate; plate-side engraved labels use brass-dim (5.7:1). Brass on the plate is permitted only as a hairline border.

rules.name: The Verified Pair Rule
rules.body: These pairs were computed and pass 4.5:1; edits must not regress them. On enamel — ink-on-enamel 12.4, ink-on-enamel-bright 15.0, ink-on-enamel-soft 5.8, brass 5.0, signal 8.2, stamp colours 6.7–7.9. On enamel-lit — ink-on-enamel 11.0, ink-on-enamel-soft 5.1, signal 7.3. On plate — plate-ink 12.8, plate-ink-soft 5.7, brass-dim 5.7, stamp colours 4.9–5.6. Signal-ink on the amber control 8.7, and on its hover fill 10.7.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo labels and titles; Literata reads. If a block is a sentence a person would say aloud, it is serif; if it is a name the instrument stamped on itself, it is condensed uppercase Archivo.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Every text block carries an explicit character cap sized to its role: 24ch section titles, 30ch footer pitch, 34ch range ledes, 46–58ch publication titles, 48–66ch prose and notes, 78ch author lists. Prose never runs the full container width.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: A heading is never preceded by an eyebrow, kicker or section number. The engraved label is a standalone caption in its own column or above a block — never a label-over-title stack.

rules.name: The Sticky Budget Rule
rules.body: Three layers can stick at once — the header, the year index, the year heading. --chrome-h (3.3rem) and --index-h (2.3rem) exist so each layer offsets by the sum of the ones above it: the index sticks at var(--chrome-h), year headings at calc(var(--chrome-h) + var(--index-h)). Both values change at 720px (5.2rem / 2.1rem) because the chrome wraps to two rows there. Any change to the header's height or wrap behaviour must update these tokens in the same edit, and the mobile year index is forced to a single non-wrapping scroll row precisely so its height stays knowable.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Band Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds go on the section, never on .chassis. A band that paints only to the container edge breaks the chassis illusion.

rules.name: The Honest Hardware Rule
rules.body: The instrument is drawn, not simulated. Flat fills, real 1px borders, one offset shadow on the one control. No multi-stop metallic gradients, no light/dark bevel pairs, no emboss, no faux screw heads.

rules.name: The Hairline Depth Rule
rules.body: When two things need separating, use a rule — 1px brass-dim or enamel-edge between rows and cards, 2px brass under a heading that opens a section. Shadow is not a separator here.

dos: Do alternate chassis and plate, and put anything a visitor must read at length on a plate.
Do reserve amber for live state, lab-led publications and the single mailto control.
Do draw every rule, divider and graduation in brass or brass-dim at 1px, or 2px when it opens a section.
Do use brass-dim, not brass, for any text on a plate (brass fails contrast there at 2.8:1).
Do print the calibration stamp on every software item, in the author's own vocabulary, including DEPRECATED.
Do update --chrome-h / --index-h in the same edit as any change to the header's height or wrapping, and keep the mobile year index a single non-wrapping row.
Do give each text block an explicit ch cap sized to its role.
Do paint band backgrounds on the section element and constrain only the inner .chassis.
Do derive graphics from real data, so removing the data removes the graphic.
Do wrap every animation in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and hold transitions at 90–160ms.
donts: Don't introduce a third surface colour, or a card that floats free of a rule, seam or 1px seating gap.
Don't spend amber on decoration, on a heading, or on a second call to action — there is one action.
Don't add an eyebrow, kicker, or section number above a heading.
Don't build a metric strip of oversized round numbers; counts belong in the inline readout.
Don't use a Unicode character or an icon font as an icon — draw it as SVG at the chassis stroke weight, like Arrow.astro.
Don't fake hardware: no metallic gradients, embossing, or paired light/dark bevels. Depth is tonal layering, hairlines, and one offset shadow on the amber control.
Don't soften, grey out, hide, or omit a maturity stamp to make the work look more finished than it is.
Don't round a corner past 2px; the lamp is the system's only circle.
Don't let a heading, list item or link rely on colour alone for state — the navigation tick, the stamp border and the lab-led left edge each carry the state in form as well as hue.
